title: Crypto’s November Stress Test: Liquidity, Custody and the Limits of Control
dek: From exchange thefts and frozen stablecoins to election-driven legislation and a sanctioned Moscow trading venue, the same question keeps resurfacing: who can actually move the money?
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a Bitcoin coin, fractured lock, U.S. Capitol, and labeled blocks representing ETF flows, legislation, exchange security, DeFi, and sanctions.

title: The Token Unlock Calendar Has a Liquidity Problem
dek: A 90-day wave of scheduled crypto releases looks alarming on paper. But reported float, recipient behavior and buy-side depth determine whether the supply ever reaches the market.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a glowing open lock and crypto tokens beside the words The Supply Behind the Float

title: DeepBook’s Supply Question: Is the Treasury Locked or Discretionary?
dek: A reported 5.27-billion-token holder, conflicting circulation figures, and an unanswered question about who can move DEEP.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a gold vault door with an interrupted lock mechanism, representing uncertainty over DeepBook token custody and transfer restrictions.

title: Bitcoin’s Recovery Has a Ceiling—and the Evidence Is Still Divided
dek: A November 3 market snapshot showed improving short-term momentum beneath stubborn higher-timeframe resistance. The harder question is what would turn a rebound into a genuine reversal.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a rising teal pathway approaching a solid amber overhead barrier, symbolizing a Bitcoin recovery facing resistance; not a market chart.

title: The Uniswap Rebound That Failed the Liquidity Test
dek: A rally can be real and still be a bad trade. That distinction became the defining feature of Uniswap’s UNI token on November 2, when a plausible intraday recovery collided with deteriorating visible liquidity, limited room to the next resistance level, and fresh questions about the source of selling pressure.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of UNI market scrutiny alongside cautionary imagery referencing the reported Binance wallet exploit

title: Bitcoin’s Quiet Lead in a Weak Crypto Market
dek: Ether and Solana fell further, while Bitcoin’s own trend deteriorated. Relative strength, it turns out, is not the same thing as a healthy market.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of three abstract market paths separating, with a restrained gold path above teal and rust paths; not a factual price chart.

title: Bitcoin’s Price Is Not the Whole Market
dek: Ahead of November’s first US trading session, Bitcoin looked comparatively resilient. Beneath the headline price, market breadth, aggressive selling and uneven liquidation exposure told a less comfortable story.
image_alt: Abstract editorial illustration: an illuminated circular opening split by a jagged amber fault line amid layered market-like bands, symbolizing the divide between Bitcoin price and underlying market breadth.

title: The Liquidity Illusion in Crypto’s New Small-Cap Listings
dek: Five token investigations exposed the gap between reported turnover, concentrated ownership and the price at which anyone could actually exit.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of many trading-flow lines narrowing through a small opening, representing the gap between reported crypto volume and usable liquidity.

title: Bitcoin’s $78,000 Rebound Has a Missing Ingredient: Proof of Spot Demand
dek: Leverage has been coming out of the market. ETF money has turned uneven. And the most important question about the bounce remains unanswered: who is actually doing the buying?

title: Bitcoin’s Selloff Was Real. The Leverage Story Is More Complicated.
dek: The October 29 decline carried the unmistakable fingerprints of forced long liquidations. But a closer look at funding, order flow and open interest suggests a market that shed leverage during the shock—and then began rebuilding it.

title: Six Trades. Three Wallets. One Unsettling Launch.
dek: SolZFoundation arrived with a privacy-bridge story and a tiny Pump.fun market. Its first indexed trades tell a more immediate story: every observed buyer sold exactly what they bought.

title: Institutional Crypto Adoption Is Real. Token Demand Is Still on Trial.
dek: Canton Coin and Chainlink are finding their way into serious financial infrastructure. The harder question is whether that progress is creating economic demand for CC and LINK—or simply a better story to trade.

title: Bitcoin Is Holding Up. The Tape Is Less Convincing.
dek: A resilient Bitcoin, weaker altcoins, and violent pockets of turnover make a deceptively calm crypto market. The deeper story is in the divergence between relative strength and absolute momentum.

title: AERO at $0.68: The Merger Is Real. The Reversal Isn't.
dek: AERO is testing the boundary between an ordinary post-launch shakeout and a deeper repricing. The chart is beginning to stabilize, but the economics tell a more complicated story.

title: Bitcoin’s $1.2 Million Buying Imbalance—and the Reversal It Hasn’t Proven
dek: On October 26, the crypto market looked calm on the surface. Beneath that calm, spot buyers and derivatives traders were telling a more complicated story.

title: WEFT’s First Week: Who Owns the Float, Who Controls the Exit?
dek: Weft Finance has a functioning market, a public tokenomics story and a strikingly concentrated supply. The harder questions are about what the ledger proves—and what it doesn’t.

title: VIRTUAL’s Apparent Alpha Has a Much Bigger Risk Story
dek: A short-window momentum model looks surprisingly good. The underlying token is also unusually volatile, heavily exposed to Bitcoin, and far from passing the tests that would make that result trustworthy.

title: RUNE’s Quiet Repricing Problem: A Real Network, an Unsettled Token Thesis
dek: THORChain is still moving meaningful value across chains. Its token is a fraction of its former price. The gap is intriguing—but the case for a recovery is more complicated than either number suggests.

title: PYTH’s Revenue Breakthrough Meets a 2.125 Billion Token Unlock
dek: A real financial-data business is emerging behind PYTH. The harder question is whether its new token-buying mechanism can mature quickly enough to matter before May 2027.

title: Venice AI’s Privacy Promise Has a Verification Problem
dek: The encryption is meaningful. The assurances are not uniform. And even a genuinely private AI product still has to prove why its token should capture the value.

title: Who Actually Benefits From Crypto Buybacks? EDGE, STONK and the Missing Ledger
dek: EDGE and STONK put two very different revenue stories on the same balance sheet. The harder question is how much economic value survives the journey from customer fees to each circulating token—and what the market has already priced in.
